group.title: School and learning
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: A number or letter a teacher gives to show how good your work is.
examples: I got a good {mark} on my spelling test.
wrong: She got the top mark because all her answers were wrong.

words.meaning: The study of numbers, shapes and amounts.
examples: We do {math} problems with a calculator.
wrong: In math class, we learn to paint pictures of flowers.

words.meaning: The study of the natural world by testing and watching carefully.
examples: In {science} class, we tested how fast ice melts.
wrong: Science is the study of old poems and songs.

words.meaning: The study of things that happened in the past.
examples: Our {history} teacher told us about ancient Rome.
wrong: In history, we learn what will happen next year.

words.meaning: The study of countries, mountains, rivers and maps.
examples: We learned the names of rivers in {geography}.
wrong: In geography, we only study numbers and sums.

words.meaning: The science of living things like plants and animals.
examples: In {biology}, we looked at a leaf under a microscope.
wrong: Biology is the study of rocks and metals, not living things.

words.meaning: The science of what things are made of and how they mix and change.
examples: We mixed two liquids in {chemistry} and they turned blue.
wrong: In chemistry class, we learn to play the violin.

words.meaning: The science of energy, movement, light and force.
examples: In {physics}, we learned why things fall to the ground.
wrong: Physics is the study of famous writers and their books.

words.meaning: A punishment where a student must stay at school after classes end.
examples: He got {detention} for talking during the test.
wrong: She got detention as a prize for her great work.

words.meaning: The person in charge of a school.
examples: The {principal} spoke to all the students in the hall.
wrong: The principal is the youngest child in the first class.

words.meaning: The big test at the end of a course or school year.
examples: I am studying hard for my {final exam} in math.
wrong: We take the final exam on the first day of the course.

words.meaning: One of the parts the school year is divided into.
examples: The summer {term} ends in June.
wrong: The school term lasts only one minute.

words.meaning: A school where people study after high school.
examples: My brother is studying art at {college}.
wrong: Children go to college before they can read.

words.meaning: A paper that tells parents how well a student is doing at school.
examples: Her {report card} showed top marks in math.
wrong: The report card tells you today’s weather.

words.meaning: A short break in the school day when children can play.
examples: We play soccer outside during {recess}.
wrong: During recess, students sit their hardest exam.

words.meaning: A class or school for children of about five, before regular school starts.
examples: My little sister started {kindergarten} this year.
wrong: Students go to kindergarten after they finish college.

words.meaning: A school for children from about six to eleven years old.
examples: She learned to read at {elementary school}.
wrong: People go to elementary school after they finish university.

words.meaning: A school for teenagers, usually from about fourteen to eighteen.
examples: He played basketball in {high school}.
wrong: My two-year-old son goes to high school.

words.meaning: A short test the teacher gives without warning.
examples: The teacher gave us a {pop quiz} on today’s reading.
wrong: We knew about the pop quiz for weeks before it happened.

words.meaning: The mark or score you get in a test or exam.
examples: I will get my exam {results} next week.
wrong: She got her result before she took the test.

words.meaning: Stories, poems and plays, studied as a school subject.
examples: In {literature} class, we are reading a famous novel.
wrong: In literature class, we only solve number problems.

words.meaning: A visit a class makes to a place outside school to learn.
examples: Our class went on a {field trip} to the science museum.
wrong: On our field trip, we stayed in the classroom all day.

words.meaning: A bus that takes children to and from school.
examples: The {school bus} picks me up at seven thirty.
wrong: The school bus takes office workers to the airport.

words.meaning: The day or ceremony when you finish your studies and get a degree.
examples: My parents came to my {graduation} last May.
wrong: Graduation is your first day at a new school.

words.meaning: A person who is studying a subject or skill.
examples: This dictionary is made for English {learners}.
wrong: She is a learner of French, so she has never studied it.

words.meaning: A language that is not spoken in your own country.
examples: Spanish is the first {foreign language} I studied.
wrong: My foreign language is the one I spoke at home as a baby.

words.meaning: The teaching and studying that happens at school and college.
examples: A good {education} can help you find a good job.
wrong: She never went to school, so she had a long education.

words.meaning: Putting a lot of effort into your work.
examples: She is a {hardworking} student who studies every evening.
wrong: He is very hardworking and never does his homework.

words.meaning: Able to speak a language easily and well.
examples: After two years in Paris, he is {fluent} in French.
wrong: She is fluent in Japanese but can’t say a single word.

words.meaning: A room in a school where students buy and eat lunch.
examples: We eat lunch in the school {cafeteria} at noon.
wrong: We sleep in the cafeteria at night and never eat there.

words.meaning: A school subject about people, history, countries and society.
examples: In {social studies}, we learned how our city is run.
wrong: Social studies is a subject where you learn to swim.

words.meaning: A school subject where students do sports and exercise.
examples: We play volleyball in {physical education}.
wrong: In physical education, we sit still and read all hour.

words.meaning: A small machine that does sums for you.
examples: You can use a {calculator} for the hard sums.
wrong: He used a calculator to wash his clothes.

words.meaning: A building where students live and sleep at a college.
examples: First-year students live in the {dormitory} on campus.
wrong: The dormitory is where students eat but never sleep.

words.meaning: A kind of test question where you pick one correct answer from a list.
examples: The exam has twenty {multiple choice} questions.
wrong: In a multiple choice test, there are never any answers to pick from.

words.meaning: To stay away from a lesson on purpose when you should go.
examples: He {skipped class} to go to the beach.
wrong: She skipped class and sat in the front row the whole lesson.

words.meaning: The months when schools are open, from the first day to the last.
examples: The {school year} starts in September.
wrong: The school year lasts for one week.

words.meaning: Helping you learn something.
examples: We watched an {educational} video about the moon.
wrong: The program was very educational; nobody learned anything.

words.meaning: A set of lessons you take on the internet.
examples: He took an {online course} in cooking.
wrong: An online course meets only in a classroom with no computers.

words.meaning: An event where students show science projects they have made.
examples: Her volcano model won first prize at the {science fair}.
wrong: At the science fair, students sell old clothes and toys.
